India’s impressive run in badminton at the Asian Games suffered a double setback on Sunday as Treesa Jolly-Gayatri Gopichand and Dhruv Kapila-Tanisha Crasto bowed out in the quarterfinals after spirited fights against higher-ranked opponents.Treesa and Gayatri, who arrived at the Games on the back of a historic bronze medal at the World Championships in New Delhi last month, went down 18-21, 9-21 to Malaysian world No. 5 pair Pearly Tan and Thinaah Muralitharan.The Indians were competitive in the opening game and matched their Malaysian opponents for long periods, but a series of errors in the second game allowed the world No. 5 pair to take control and seal a straight-game victory.The Indians had entered the tournament in impressive form, having already registered two wins over the world No. 3 Japanese combination of Yuki Fukushima and Mayu Matsumoto. However, they faced a difficult challenge against Pearly and Thinaah, having lost six of their previous eight meetings against the Malaysian duo.The Malaysians made the early running, opening up an 8-3 lead, but Treesa and Gayatri responded strongly to level the score at 10-10.The contest then turned into an intense attacking battle, with both pairs trading points and remaining locked at 14-14.Pearly and Thinaah subsequently capitalised on errors from the Indians to move 17-14 ahead. Gayatri produced a clever deception at the net and the Malaysians sent a shot wide, giving the Indians hope of another comeback.But Pearly and Thinaah maintained their composure to move to 19-16 before Treesa found the net, handing them four game points. The Indians saved two, but a powerful smash from the Malaysian pair ended the opening game 21-18. Treesa and Gayatri started the second game brightly, moving 3-0 ahead after the change of ends. The Malaysians, however, quickly turned the momentum around by forcing errors from the Indian pair and surged to a 7-3 lead.The gap widened further as the Indians struggled to find their rhythm, with Pearly and Thinaah racing to an 11-4 advantage. The Malaysian pair continued to pile on the pressure and moved 13-6 ahead. With Treesa and Gayatri unable to arrest the flow of points, Pearly and Thinaah soon earned 12 match points. Pearly then hit the net, but Gayatri sent the next shot wide to hand the Malaysians a 21-9 win and a place in the semifinals.Earlier, Dhruv Kapila and Tanisha Crasto produced a spirited performance against world No. 1 Chinese pair Feng Yan Zhe and Huang Dongping but eventually went down 14-21, 21-18, 18-21. The Indian mixed doubles pair struggled in the opening game as the Chinese combination established control and took a 21-14 lead.Kapila and Crasto responded brilliantly in the second game, raising their intensity and forcing the contest into a decider after securing a 21-18 win. The Indians continued to battle hard in the deciding game, but Feng and Huang held their nerve in the crucial moments to close out the match 21-18.India's campaign in the singles events remains alive, with two-time Olympic medallist PV Sindhu and young Unnati Hooda set to feature in their respective women's singles quarterfinals later on Sunday. Sindhu will take on China's Chen Yu Fei, while Unnati will face Japan's Akane Yamaguchi as the Indian duo look to keep the country's medal hopes alive.
Article Summary: Treesa Jolly-Gayatri Gopichand and Dhruv Kapila-Tanisha Crasto beaten by world No. 5 pair Pearly Tan and Thinaah Muralitharan. Indian duo had entered the tournament in impressive form, having already registered two wins over the world no. 3 Japanese combination of Yuki Fukushima and Mayu Matsumoto. India's campaign in the singles events remains alive, with PV Sindhu and young Unnati Hooda set to feature in their respective women's singles quarterfinals later on Sunday.

Article Title: Asian Games 2026 Day 7: India win seven medals as kabaddi teams deliver gold double in action-packed Saturday
Article Text:
L-R: Joshna Chinappa, Prachi Choudhary and Tajinderpal Singh Toor

Barwal delivers historic marathon silver

ALSO READ:

Kabaddi teams maintain their grip on gold

Shooting and athletics add three more medals

Anahat, Abhay keep squash gold hopes alive

Hockey, archery provide further positives

Mixed fortunes in badminton and table tennis

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India enjoyed one of its most productive days at the Asian Games 2026 on Saturday, winning seven medals with the kabaddi teams providing the biggest highlights by successfully defending their respective gold medals.The men defeated Iran 40-34 in a hard-fought final, while the women also overcame Iran 37-34 to complete a memorable kabaddi gold double for India. The men's triumph was their ninth Asian Games gold in the sport, while the women's victory brought their tally to four.India's seven-medal haul also included a historic silver for marathon runner Sawan Barwal, silver medals for Tajinderpal Singh Toor and the women's 50m rifle 3 positions team, and bronze medals for Prachi Choudhary in the women's 400m and Joshna Chinappa-Velavan Senthilkumar in squash.The day's results took India's overall medal tally to 30 — four gold, 12 silver and 14 bronze.The day began with one of India's biggest surprises when Sawan Barwal produced a stunning run to win silver in the men's marathon and break his own national record.The 28-year-old Armyman from Mandi, Himachal Pradesh, completed the 42.195km race in 2 hours, 11 minutes and 37 seconds to finish behind Japan's Ichitaka Yamashita, who won gold in 2:10:49.China's Peiyou Feng took bronze in 2:12:13.Barwal's silver was India's first Asian Games marathon medal since Hosur Kukkappa Seetharan's bronze in the 1982 edition in New Delhi. He also became only the fourth Indian marathon runner to win an Asian Games medal.Chhota Singh had won gold and Surat Singh Mathur bronze at the inaugural Asian Games in 1951, while Seetharan's bronze came three decades later.India's kabaddi campaign once again ended with both teams on top of the podium, although neither final was straightforward.The women held their nerve to beat Iran 37-34, while the men recovered from a closely fought first half to defeat the same opponents 40-34.The men's gold was India's ninth in the sport at the Asian Games, underlining their long-standing dominance, while the women's team retained the title they had won at Hangzhou.The two victories accounted for India's only gold medals of the day and provided a major boost to the country's medal count.At the shooting range, Tilottama Sen, Vidarsa Vinod and Ashi Chouksey won silver in the women's 50m rifle 3 positions team event.The Indian trio aggregated 1763 points to finish behind China, who set a Games Record of 1773 for gold. Kazakhstan took bronze with 1754.Tilottama and Vidarsa also reached the individual final but narrowly missed the podium, finishing fourth and fifth respectively.In athletics, Prachi Choudhary added a bronze in the women's 400m, clocking 53.21 seconds. Bahrain's Salwa Naser won gold in a Games Record 49.20 seconds, while Iran's Zahra Zarei Manoujan took silver in 52.38 seconds.There was disappointment too, as two-time defending champion Tajinderpal Singh Toor had to settle for silver in the men's shot put. His 20.64m throw was well below his personal best of 21.77m.Iran's Mohammadreza Tayebise won gold with a Games Record 20.81m, breaking Toor's previous Games mark of 20.75m.India's squash campaign received a major boost as Anahat Singh and Abhay Singh stormed into their respective singles finals.The 18-year-old Anahat produced one of the biggest wins of her career, coming from 0-2 down to stun world No. 6 Satomi Watanabe of Japan 9-11, 11-13, 12-10, 11-6, 11-3.Abhay followed by sweeping Pakistan's Muhammad Irfan 11-3, 12-10, 11-6 to reach the men's final.A gold for either player would also bring the prospect of qualification for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, where squash will make its debut.Joshna Chinappa and Velavan Senthilkumar had earlier secured India's bronze in mixed doubles after losing 1-2 to Hong Kong's Tang Ming Hong and Lee Ka Yi.The men's hockey team reached the semifinals after beating Japan 2-0 in its penultimate pool match.India also made a strong start to its archery campaign. Dhiraj Bommadevara topped the men's recurve individual qualification with 698 points, setting a new Asian Games qualification record. Chikitha Taniparthi topped the women's compound qualification with 705 points.India also finished first in compound mixed team qualification.Young shuttler Unnati Hooda produced one of India's standout performances in badminton, winning two matches to reach the women's singles quarterfinals.The 19-year-old first defeated Malaysia's Ling Ching Wong 21-14, 20-22, 21-19 before stunning world No. 6 Putri Kusuma Wardani of Indonesia 21-19, 21-13. She will face Japan's Akane Yamaguchi in the quarterfinals.Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand also advanced after beating Japan's world No. 3 pair Mayu Matsumoto and Yuki Fukushima 24-22, 21-18.However, Lakshya Sen and Ayush Shetty were knocked out.India's table tennis campaign ended without further medals after Manush Shah and Yashaswini Ghorpade lost their respective singles pre-quarterfinals. India finished with one TT medal — the mixed doubles bronze won by Manush and Diya Chitale.The day also brought limited returns in esports, fencing and canoeing.
Article Summary: India enjoyed one of its most productive days at the Asian Games 2026. The kabaddi teams provided the biggest highlights by successfully defending their respective gold medals. The men defeated Iran 40-34 in a hard-fought final, while the women also overcame Iran 37-34. India's seven-medal haul also included a historic silver for marathon runner Sawan Barwal.

Article Title: 'Khali pet gold jita hai': Why India's kabaddi team did not eat before Asian Games final
Article Text:
Reuters Photo

‘Those 40 minutes were important’

India turn the final around

Keeping an eye on India’s medal tally

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Gold medal dedicated to coach

‘Japan has created history for me’

India’s men’s kabaddi team had one thing on their mind before the Asian Games final - winning gold.So much so that the players did not eat properly before their title clash against Iran.“Khali pet gold jita hai,” captain Pawan Sehrawat said after India defeated Iran 40-34 to retain their Asian Games men’s kabaddi title on Saturday.India had prepared well for the final, but Pawan knew the result would only be decided on the mat.“I was very excited about the match. I was very excited about what was going to happen in the match in the evening. Even if we know that we are playing well, we have practised well. But until the result comes, it stays in the mind. Those 40 minutes were important,” Pawan told IANS.India went into half-time trailing 17-18 but produced a strong second-half performance to turn the match around.Arjun Deshwal and Devank Dalal led the attack, while Sumit and Jaideep played important roles in defence.With 10 minutes left, India moved five points ahead after Arjun got past Iran captain Fazel Atrachali and helped India inflict an All-Out.Sumit then made an important tackle on Amirmohammad Zafar Danesh, while Rahul Sethpal also made a key defensive contribution late in the match.The win completed India's unbeaten campaign and gave them their ninth Asian Games gold medal in men's kabaddi.For Pawan, however, the wait for the result made the final even more emotional.“Everyone is emotional, so I get emotional at such moments. And it was that once the 40 minutes are over, we will eat and drink well. Not just one, but after that gold has come,” he said.Pawan also revealed that the players were following India's position on the medal table during the Games.“We were seeing on the way that if our two golds are added, then where will we go? Till that time, as far as I could see, we were in sixth. And since then, we have not used the mobile properly. I don't know which number we will have in our medal tally,” he said.Pawan credited his coach Randhir Sehrawat for playing a major role in his success and dedicated the gold medal to him.“I would like to dedicate it to my coach Randhir Sehrawat. Because it is because of him that this medal has come to me,” he said.He also urged the government to consider Randhir for the Dronacharya Award, pointing out that several Arjuna Award winners had trained under him.Pawan, who was one of India’s flag-bearers at the opening ceremony alongside Manu Bhaker, also spoke about his experience in Japan.“Japan is very beautiful. For me, Japan has created history. I was a flag bearer. I was with such a good athlete, Manu Bhaker. For me, it is a miracle,” he said.
Article Summary: India defeated Iran 40-34 to retain their Asian Games men’s kabaddi title. Captain Pawan Sehrawat dedicated the gold medal to his coach Randhir. India went into half-time trailing 17-18 but produced a strong second-half performance.

Article Title: India’s kabaddi double! Men beat Iran to defend gold after women’s triumph at Asian Games

Team India after winning kabaddi gold. (X Photo)

NEW DELHI: India completed a golden double in kabaddi at the Asian Games 2026 on Saturday as the men’s team defeated Iran 40-34 in a thrilling final, hours after the women had also beaten the same opponents to retain their title.The men’s victory at Aichi-Nagoya earned India its ninth Asian Games gold in men’s kabaddi and successfully defended the title won at the Hangzhou edition. The two kabaddi gold medals also lifted India’s overall medal tally to 28 — four gold, 11 silver and 13 bronze, taking the country into the top 10 of the standings.It was another tense encounter against Iran, the 2018 Asian Games champions, with neither side able to establish sustained control for long periods. But India held their nerve through a roller-coaster second half before pulling away late to secure the gold.The final began on an even note, with the teams locked at 5-5 after the opening eight minutes. India then managed to create a small advantage, moving 12-9 ahead, but Iran responded strongly and turned the contest around.With less than five minutes remaining in the first half, Iran moved ahead 14-13. India responded by reclaiming the advantage at 16-14, only for Iran to strike back again.The momentum continued to swing between the two sides, and Iran eventually went into the interval with an 18-17 lead.India needed a strong response after the restart, but Iran extended their advantage to 20-17. A crucial super tackle helped India cut the deficit to 19-20 before the defending champions finally regained the lead at 21-20.Iran immediately levelled at 21-21, underlining just how little separated the two teams.India then began to build some breathing room, moving 24-21 ahead. Iran responded with a super tackle of their own to collect two points and reduce India's advantage to 24-23.The match remained finely balanced, but India produced the crucial breakthrough with an all-out that pushed them five points clear at 29-24 with 10 minutes remaining.From there, India managed the contest effectively. Iran continued to push for a comeback, but the Indian defence held firm and the attack kept adding points to maintain the advantage.India eventually closed out the final 40-34 to complete the kabaddi double and retain the men's title.The result also gave India its fourth gold of the Games and moved the country into the top 10 of the overall medal standings.Earlier on Saturday, the Indian women's kabaddi team had set the stage for the double by overcoming Iran 37-34 in another closely fought final.The women, too, successfully defended the gold they had won at Hangzhou. India held their nerve during a tense closing phase as Iran attempted to force a late comeback.With only a minute remaining, Iran needed points to remain in contention, but India's defence produced a crucial tackle on Aynaz to effectively seal the contest.India eventually prevailed 37-34, with Sanju Devi once again playing a key role after being one of the team's standout performers throughout the tournament.For Indian kabaddi, it was a statement day: two finals against Iran, two victories and two gold medals, with both the men's and women's teams successfully defending their Asian Games titles.
Article Summary: Men follow women to complete golden double in kabaddi at Asian Games 2026. Men's team defeat Iran 40-34 in a thrilling final in Aichi-Nagoya. Hours earlier, the women's team beat Iran 37-34 to retain their title.

Article Title: OFFSIDE | Retrospective titles for Man Utd, Arsenal and Liverpool? What Man City's 'guilty' verdict means for the Premier League and the UK government
Article Text:
Sergio Agüero celebrates the goal that delivered Manchester City their first Premier League title in 2012, the moment that announced the arrival of a new footballing empire.

Aguerooooo (13 May 2012)

Ted Lasso

What exactly is City guilty of?

What are the likeliest punishments?

The Pep legacy issue

Sir Alex Ferguson and Pep Guardiola together, two managers who have defined very different versions of Premier League dominance and whose legacies now sit at the heart of the debate over Manchester City’s era.

Beyond football

FILE - Manchester City's head coach Pep Guardiola hugs Ruben Dias, left and Bernardo Silva afterthe English Premier League soccer match between Manchester City and Manchester United in Manchester, England, Sunday, April 6, 2025. (AP Photo/Dave Thompson, File)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

dream

Inception

Hello and welcome to a special edition of Offside, where we make sense of the ‘guilty verdict’ against Manchester City on 114 out of 115 charges, decode what it means for the Premier League, question where it leaves Pep Guardiola’s legacy, wonder if other Premier League clubs will get retrospective titles, and look at what it means beyond football for the Premier League, the UK and the UAE.The idea of neutrality in journalism, particularly sports journalism, is a preposterous one. Like secularism or having just one beer, it’s the adult version of believing Santa Claus is real. Ergo, it’s almost impossible to have a detached view of what it means for a lifelong Manchester United fan – even accounting for the post-colonial absurdity of supporting a club in the land of one’s former oppressors – to find City guilty. The same goes for any other football fan who has been on the receiving end of City’s “sportswashed” total football.But for United fans, to truly understand the hurt, one needs to go back to 13 May 2012.United were playing Sunderland at the Stadium of Light and Rooney scored the only goal. As the match ended, the United players waited for the result from the Etihad, where City were trailing QPR 1-2 in injury time. And then Dzeko and Aguero scored, giving City their first Premier League title, a moment that, with the benefit of hindsight, was the day the balance of power shifted in Mancunian football.For City fans, it was the reward of supporting the club through thick and thin, through years of heartbreak as their storied rivals marched from title to title while they flirted with relegation or turned up against Macclesfield or Stockport.Aguero’s goal wasn’t a flash in the pan but the first shot for City’s new empire. The club started to resemble the football version of the United States, attracting the world’s best talent, including Yaya Toure, David Silva, Kevin De Bruyne, and eventually Erling Haaland. Along came Pep Guardiola, football’s most coveted manager, under whom City became the definitive football team of their age, highlighted by the fact that they were often the pantomime villains in. In 2013, the City Football Group became the mothership of a dozen clubs spanning five continents including New York City FC in America, Girona in Spain and Mumbai City FC in India. Aguero’s goal became for City what Ralph Waldo Emerson described inas the “first shot heard around the world”, signalling the arrival of football’s newest and richest empire.Given City’s hegemony over the last decade, there was a collective schadenfreudegasm after the first report about the guilty verdict was published. The reactions came in thick and fast on Football Twitter and other forums, which collectively turned up to dance on City’s proverbial grave.Manchester United legend Rio Ferdinand wondered how many titles that would give him. David De Gea also wanted the same conversation. Arsenal’s most pestiferous fan Piers Morgan argued that “at the very minimum they must be relegated from the Premier League and stripped of all fraudulently ‘won’ titles.”In the past, Jose Mourinho has jested about getting his medal and bonus for winning the league when he finished second with Manchester United. Former Liverpool manager Jurgen Klopp, often ending up on the wrong end in the battles against Pep Guardiola, has said he will buy beers and celebrate.Memes imagine the new City crest as a sinking ship , Salman Khan in a United jersey saying “It’s Done, Bro”, while Americans got trolled for not understanding why Zohran Mamdani was tweeting: 114. A clip from– a nifty football drama about Brian Clough’s disastrous 44-day ordeal at Leeds United – has rival fans reminding City : “The first thing you can do for me is to chuck all your medals… into the biggest dustbin you can find because you have not won any of them fairly.”But beyond the jokes, there are wider questions about what this means, for which we have to ask ourselves:Mainstreaming Oasis? Yes.Spending the GDP of a small nation and claiming it as football heritage? Yes, too.Sportswashing? Probably, but what else is sports for?Playing football so tactically conformist that it shunted individualists? Jack Grealish would agree.City’s financial irregularities, the sort of thing Arsene Wenger had called “financial doping”, came to light when German magazinepublished internal Man City emails – football’s equivalent of the Epstein emails – that appeared to show money coming from Sheikh Mansour and Abu Dhabi being presented as independent sponsorship revenue.Financial Fair Play (FFP) – something City fans believed was brought in to benefit the ‘Red Cartel’ (all its direct rivals were red) – was ostensibly designed to ensure a modicum of an even playing field by limiting how much owners could simply pump into clubs and asking clubs to earn the money that they spend through sponsorships, which was always dicey when the owners are sponsors too.The clearest example of that dichotomy came from the blue half of Manchester.One internal email suggested that of a £67.5 million sponsorship payment, Etihad would provide only £8 million while £59.5 million would come from ADUG, Sheikh Mansour’s ownership vehicle. City disputed that interpretation and later won at CAS, which ruled UEFA had not proved the allegation, although City were still fined €10 million for failing to cooperate.But there were more awkward emails.In 2012-13, City’s finance chief pointed out that sacking Roberto Mancini would leave them £9.9 million short of FFP compliance. After City lost the FA Cup final and missed out on a sponsor bonus, Abu Dhabi-linked sponsorship payments were reportedly adjusted, with City Football Group board member Simon Pearce doing his best Trump impression and writing: “Of course. We can do what we want.”Mancini presented another issue. The former City manager was reportedly earning £1.45 million a year from City, while also receiving another £1.75 million annually through a consultancy contract with Al Jazira, another club controlled by Sheikh Mansour. The allegation was that the second payment was effectively additional City remuneration that should have been disclosed.Similar questions surrounded player pay and image-rights arrangements. The allegations also included owner-linked money masquerading as sponsorship revenue, player/image-rights costs kept off City’s normal books, sponsorship payments adjusted when City were short and non-cooperation with the Premier League investigation. The bulk of the charges, however, related to inaccurate financial information and non-cooperation.The obvious analogy here is to Italian football’s Calciopoli scandal involving corruption in refereeing and football administration that saw Juventus relegated to the second division. While the 2004-05 championship was left vacant, the 2005-06 title was given to Inter Milan.That has obviously led many to wonder if something similar will happen in the Premier League. If that were the case, then the clubs that finished second could get the titles in that era, including Manchester United, Liverpool and Arsenal.Various clubs, including Manchester United, are also assessing the financial losses incurred during that era, but the bigger problem perhaps is for one of the Premier League’s greatest dynasties. The revelations put a huge question mark on everything: Aguerooooo. City finishing with 100 points. The Guardiola and Klopp rivalry. The Treble.The corruption scandal hit Italian football quite hard, although Italy went on to win the 2006 World Cup and qualify in 2010 and 2014 before missing 2018 and 2022. Could something similar happen here?Now, short of getting amind-zapping device, football memories, sad or happy, cannot be erased.No Manchester United fan will forget Ole Gunnar Solskjaer poking it in against Bayern Munich in Barcelona. Similarly, nothing Messrs Aguero, Kompany, Silva or De Bruyne have done can be negated. But would those talented world-beaters even have been there if FFP rules had been followed? Even if City’s verdict survives the appeal, the shadow cast over the most successful Premier League team of the last decade will hang heavy like an albatross around its neck.While former players and managers might have dreams of retrospective titles, that’s unlikely to pass. The likeliest punishment is a massive points deduction that would potentially relegate City.Football finance expert Kieran Maguire told the BBC that rival clubs would “expect some form of points deduction”, while former City chairman David Bernstein argued that just a fine would be “pointless”. A fine, and a humongous one at that, might be in the offing. Rival clubs, including Manchester United, are considering compensation claims for lost prize money, Champions League qualification and commercial revenue. Unfortunately for fans of rival clubs, the stripping of historic titles and handing them over is the least likely outcome, and there is, according to BBC Sport, “little appetite for that” either from the Premier League or rival clubs.When Pep Guardiola left City, ESPN’s Mark Ogden wrote a piece arguing that his legacy ought to be held higher than Sir Alex Ferguson’s because he edged the Scotsman as the greatest manager of the Premier League era amid various variables.One obviously disagreed.There’s an anecdotal quote often attributed to Jose Mourinho: “I don’t coach teams where the kitman could win the league.” While that’s not true for Barcelona, where he had the world’s greatest footballer at his disposal – though some could argue that Messi perhaps wouldn’t have become Messi without Guardiola’s tutelage – that’s true of Bayern Munich and Manchester City.Unlike Mourinho, who won the Champions League with Porto, or Ferguson, who broke the Old Firm hegemony in Scotland with Aberdeen before taking a relegation-threatened Manchester United to the pinnacle of English and European football, Guardiola has always helmed the biggest team in the land with the biggest budget that might not have been fairly held together.In the past, Guardiola has claimed that if the Man City hierarchy lied to him about the irregularities, he would walk. But the Spaniard is already gone, and one wonders if, perhaps like all the greatest magicians, Pep picked the perfect time to exit before the iceberg emerged.Given that the Premier League is the UK’s greatest export since opium and the Beatles, the ramifications of any punishment will also be huge.City is owned by Sheikh Mansour, a member of Abu Dhabi’s ruling family and the UAE’s Vice-President and Deputy Prime Minister, which means that any existential punishment will reverberate beyond football given Britain’s relationship with the wealthy Gulf state and the fact that Emirati money is deeply embedded in both Manchester and the UK.In a statement published on Man City’s website, Chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak wrote that the club had “faced challenges together before and prevailed” and added: “There remain many who want to undermine the momentum of our Club. We will not give them that opportunity.”The timing couldn’t be worse for Manchester as a city that is having its brightest moment under the sun since the Industrial Revolution, with the “King of the North” Andy Burnham, the former Greater Manchester mayor, taking over as UK PM and Manchester at the centre of his devolution pitch.In July, one of his first conversations as Prime Minister was with UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed, a dialogue that began with a thank you for the UAE’s investment in Manchester and the “incredible impact” it had on the city.The City Football Group says more than £700 million of private investment has gone into East Manchester and the Etihad Campus, while the Manchester Life partnership between Abu Dhabi United Group and Manchester City Council began as a £1 billion housing initiative.UK-UAE trade was about £25 billion in 2025, with more than 5,000 British companies operating in the Emirates, and the UAE has billions invested in Britain. Britain also concluded a new trade agreement with the Gulf states in May, which the government estimates could eventually add £3.7 billion a year to the UK economy.Ergo, City getting relegated might just become one of the bigger fiducial headaches for the UK since its Empire collapsed after World War II.And it would have further ramifications for all Premier League clubs, the majority of which are foreign-owned. Punishing City could scare away massive investors, but failing to punish them would mean that anyone is free to flout the financial rules.And what would the fans think if the competition were compromised? Would the 1.45 billion people who watched live Premier League football in 2024-25 continue to do so? Would people across time zones get up at ungodly hours to follow the trials and travails of footballers in a league that is deemed venal and corrupt?The verdict will be a litmus test for the Premier League and the UK government. Irrespective of the outcome, City will always epitomise what global capital can do to English football. After years of wooing global capital, the UK will now need to walk a tightrope and see if it can regulate that capital, or if it even remains in a position to dictate terms.Perhaps like Americans, City fans too had started believing in their own exceptionalism that didn’t require them to follow the rules.Like Martin Luther King Jr, Man City fans too had a. Earlier, it used to be simply to beat United in the Manchester derby. When Agüero scored, they dreamt they could beat their storied neighbours in the league race. Man City became the kings of England and Europe, the definitive Premier League team of the last decade. If the findings survive appeal, the greatest era in the club’s history will forever carry an asterisk. For decades, City fans dreamed of waking up from United’s shadow. After a decade of doing exactly that, they will now be forced to ask the same question Dom Cobb had to ask in: Was it a dream or was it real?
Article Summary: Manchester City have been found guilty of 114 out of 115 charges of financial misconduct. The club has been accused of breaking the Financial Fair Play rules. City won their first Premier League title in 2012 with a 2-1 victory over Manchester United at the Etihad Stadium. Sergio Agüero’s goal was the ‘first shot heard around the world’, signalling the arrival of a new football empire.

Article Title: ‘They cannot take out of us’: Rodri breaks silence as former club Man City face losing three Premier League titles
Article Text:
Rodri has defended former club Manchester City after their 114-charge verdict, insisting their achievements cannot simply be erased.

Rodri stands by City's innocence

Rodri says City's achievements cannot be taken away

Manchester City maintain their position

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Rodri has become the first prominent former Manchester City player to publicly address the club's 114-charge verdict, and the former midfielder is standing firmly behind his old side. City were found guilty of 114 of the 115 Premier League financial rule breaches brought against them, but Rodri says he continues to believe the club are innocent and will wait for the legal process to run its course.Speaking at a press conference ahead of Spain's Nations League match against England, Rodri was asked about the verdict after the independent commission found City guilty of the majority of the charges relating to the period between 2009 and 2018.The former City midfielder, who made 298 appearances for the club between 2019 and 2026, said the club had consistently maintained its innocence and that he had no reason to change his position.“They always express the confidence that they never did something wrong, and we believe in that,” Rodri said.“Until the moment they are proved wrong, we will believe the club. They always tell us the confidence they have on the innocence.”Rodri then pointed to City's previous experience with UEFA's financial regulations as a reason for maintaining that position.City were initially given a two-year ban from European competitions by UEFA in February 2020 after being found to have committed “serious breaches” of UEFA's club licensing and financial fair play regulations. The Court of Arbitration for Sport later overturned the ban after City appealed, although the club were still fined €10 million for failing to cooperate with UEFA's investigation.Rodri said the episode influenced the way he views the current Premier League case.“We had the example of 2020 that the process was the same, and at the end nothing happened,” he explained.“We have faced something similar; we had a similar judicial process – different accusation, but similar process.“There as well, in the first instance, we were found guilty, but we believed in the club and the innocence that the club maintained, and in the end we ended up acquitted.“So, I believe in the justice system, and I believe in the innocence of the club.”City were charged by the Premier League in February 2023, with the allegations covering nine seasons between 2009 and 2018. During that period, the club won three Premier League titles, three League Cups, one Community Shield and one FA Cup.The possibility of Manchester City being stripped of those Premier League titles has become one of the most contentious questions following the verdict, although no sanctions have yet been decided and City are expected to appeal.Rodri was asked directly about the possibility of the club losing its silverware and made clear that he does not believe the achievements of the players involved can simply be erased.“What we did, they cannot take out of us,” Rodri said.“It’s something that is not paid by money. It’s paid with effort, with the damage, with, you know, being shoulder to shoulder every day.”“I can tell you that everything was deserved, and I’m glad that I could live one of the best eras of English football in here.”Rodri was part of City's Premier League-winning team in 2020/21, 2021/22 and 2022/23, meaning his own honours at the club came largely after the period covered by the charges. He joined City in 2019 and left for Barcelona in 2026 after six seasons in Manchester.Manchester City responded to the verdict on Friday by reiterating that the Premier League process remains ongoing and that the club's position has not changed since the charges were brought in 2023.“The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such, Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the Club’s statement of February 2023,” the club said.“The Club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.”City have consistently denied wrongdoing since the Premier League brought the charges against them, maintaining that they possess a “body of irrefutable evidence” supporting their defence.The independent commission has yet to determine the sanctions arising from the 114 findings, while City are expected to appeal the verdict. Until that process is completed, the club's titles remain officially intact and Rodri's position is unchanged: he continues to believe Manchester City are innocent.
Article Summary: Rodri is the first prominent former Manchester City player to publicly address the club's 114-charge verdict. City were found guilty of 114 of the 115 Premier League financial rule breaches brought against them, but Rodri says he continues to believe the club are innocent. The possibility of City being stripped of those Premier League titles has become one of the most contentious questions following the verdict.

Article Title: If Manchester City are actually stripped of their three prized Premier League titles, which clubs will emerge as the new champions?
Article Text:
Manchester City won three Premier League titles during the period under investigation: 2011/12, 2013/14 and 2017/18./ Image: Manchester City

Why City's three titles are now part of the discussion

FILE - The club logo decorates a corner flag before the English Premier League soccer match between Manchester City and Newcastle United at the Etihad Stadium in Manchester, England, Saturday, Sept. 1, 2018. (AP Photo/Jon Super, File)

Could Manchester City actually lose the titles?

Pep Guardiola, the then Manager of Manchester City, poses for a photo with the Premier League title trophy following his team's victory during the Premier League match between Manchester City and West Ham United at Etihad Stadium on May 19, 2024 in Manchester, England. (Photo/Getty Images)

Which clubs finished second behind City?

2011/12 — Manchester United

2013/14 — Liverpool

2017/18 — Manchester United

2011/12: Manchester United

2013/14: Liverpool

2017/18: Manchester United

What punishment could Manchester City face?

Suspend a club from playing league matches

Points deductions

Recommend to the board that league matches be replayed

Recommend to the board that the league expels the respondent club

Order compensation

Cancel or refuse registration of players

Conditional punishment

Order the club to pay costs

Make such other order as it thinks fit

Manchester City’s reported guilty verdict on 114 of the 115 Premier League financial charges has reopened one of the biggest questions hanging over the case: if the club are eventually stripped of the titles they won during the period under investigation, who would actually be recognised as champions instead?The answer is not as straightforward as simply handing the trophies to the teams that finished second, particularly because no sanction has yet been decided, City are expected to appeal and the Premier League’s rules give an independent commission a wide range of options.Manchester City were charged by the Premier League in February 2023 with 115 alleged breaches of its financial rules covering the period from 2009 to 2018. The independent commission’s hearing began on September 16, 2024, and ran for around three months before concluding in December 2024.On Friday, September 25, 2026, The Athletic reported that the commission had found City guilty on 114 of the 115 charges. Reuters subsequently reported the same finding, while noting that the club are expected to appeal and that the process is not yet complete. Manchester City have maintained that the Premier League process remains ongoing and that their position has not changed.No sanctions have been announced, meaning the reported verdict does not itself strip City of any trophy. The next stage will determine what punishment, if any, follows, with both sides having an appeal route under the Premier League rules.The reason the titles have become part of the conversation is the period covered by the charges.City won the Premier League three times between the 2009/10 and 2017/18 seasons, claiming their first title in 44 years in 2011/12 before winning again in 2013/14 and 2017/18.The first of those triumphs came in extraordinary fashion. City finished level on points with Manchester United in 2011/12 but won the title on goal difference, with Sergio Agüero's famous 94th-minute goal against Queens Park Rangers delivering the championship at the Etihad Stadium.Two years later, City finished two points ahead of Liverpool to win the 2013/14 title. Their third championship within the period came in 2017/18, when Pep Guardiola's side became the first Premier League team to reach 100 points.That leaves three seasons in which a retrospective title change could theoretically affect the final standings, should the commission ultimately impose a sanction that alters those results.There is a legal route for retrospective sporting punishment, but that is different from saying title stripping is inevitable or even likely.Sub-clause W.51.7 of the Premier League handbook states that the commission can “impose upon the respondent any combination of the foregoing or such other penalty as it shall think fit”. According to The Athletic, the potential sanctions under Rule W.51 range from reprimands and financial penalties to points deductions and expulsion from the Premier League.The important detail is that points deductions can be imposed retrospectively, meaning the commission has a mechanism through which past league standings could potentially be affected. That is what creates the possibility, however remote, of City losing titles won during the period covered by the case.José Mourinho raised the possibility himself in October 2024, when his Manchester United side's 2017/18 campaign was brought up ahead of a Europa League meeting with Fenerbahçe.“As you know, we finished second in the Premier League [in 2018]," Mourinho said with a grin.“I think we still have a chance to win that league because maybe they punish Manchester City with points, and maybe we win that league and then they have to pay me the bonus and give me the medal.”The practical question is whether a retrospective points deduction would automatically result in another club being declared champion.Finance expert Kieran Maguire told Sky Sports in 2024 that it would be “difficult” for another club to establish that City's alleged breaches directly cost them silverware.“If you talk to lawyers, they will say it will be difficult for another club to say that they lost a title, or they lost probably more importantly access to the Champions League and the rewards that brings,” Maguire said.The issue was also discussed at the Business of Football Summit in 2025, where Sky reporter Rob Harris spoke with sports journalist Matt Hughes of FootBiz, sports lawyer Simon Leaf and The Sun reporter Martin Lipton.Hughes said: “There seems to be no appetite to take retrospective punishment.”Leaf was more cautious, saying it was still “too early” to reach a final view, while pointing to the potential financial claims from clubs that believe they missed out because of City's results.“I suspect there will be certain clubs looking at this and saying, actually we would have been entitled to payments for qualifying for Champions League... or even bonuses from sponsors from finishing in a different position,” Leaf said.Lipton, meanwhile, argued that removing the titles would go too far.“If you were to strip titles, the single most iconic moment in the history of the Premier League - Sergio Aguero's 94th minute goal against QPR to win the league - didn't happen,” he said.“You can't rewrite history to that extent.”Lipton added that title stripping was “not going to happen”.If the Premier League were to retrospectively alter the three title races in question, the runners-up provide the obvious starting point.Manchester United finished level on points with City in 2011/12, with both clubs ending the season on 89 points. City took the title on goal difference after Agüero's extraordinary late winner against QPR.Sir Alex Ferguson's United therefore represent the most obvious alternative champion if the 2011/12 title were removed from City's record.It is also the title most deeply intertwined with the debate because of how it was decided. City did not simply finish ahead of United by a comfortable margin; they were separated by goal difference after one of the most famous finishes in Premier League history.Liverpool finished second in 2013/14, two points behind City.Brendan Rodgers' side had led the title race for much of the season and appeared on course to win their first Premier League championship before a late-season collapse allowed City to overtake them.A retrospective alteration would therefore put Liverpool in the position of the team immediately behind City in the final table, although, as Maguire and the other experts have pointed out, being the original runner-up does not necessarily mean a club is automatically entitled to receive the title years later.Manchester United finished second again in 2017/18, this time 19 points behind Guardiola's record-breaking City side.Mourinho's comments in 2024 specifically referred to this season and his belief that United could still theoretically be awarded the title if City were punished retrospectively.So, if the runners-up were simply retrospectively promoted into the vacant championship places, the hypothetical list would be:That is a possible scenario rather than a confirmed outcome. There is currently no announced decision stating that these three clubs will inherit City's titles if sanctions are imposed.The reported finding of 114 guilty charges has moved the case into its next stage, but it has not established what punishment City will receive. The independent commission has a range of sanctions available under the Premier League's rules, and the club are expected to appeal the verdict.The potential punishments listed in the Premier League handbook are:For now, the three title races remain officially unchanged: Manchester City are the champions of 2011/12, 2013/14 and 2017/18. The possibility of Manchester United receiving two of those titles and Liverpool receiving the other exists only if the eventual disciplinary process produces that outcome.
Article Summary: Manchester City were charged by the Premier League in February 2023 with 115 alleged breaches of its financial rules covering the period from 2009 to 2018. The independent commission’s hearing began on September 16, 2024, and ran for around three months before concluding in December 2024. On September 25, 2026, The Athletic reported that the commission had found City guilty on 114 of the 115 charges. No sanctions have been announced, meaning the reported verdict does not itself strip City of any trophy. The next stage will determine what punishment, if any, follows.

Article Title: India impress against Panama in 1-1 draw as Blue Tigers stand firm against World Cup side
Article Text:
India hold World Cup-bound Panama to 1-1 draw in major test for Khalid Jamil’s side/ Image: X

Williams rewards India's positive first half

Panama respond, but India withstand the pressure

India now turn to Brazil and Uruguay

India had to surrender a first-half lead, but the Blue Tigers came away from Bengaluru with plenty to take from a 1-1 draw against Panama, a side ranked 94 places above them in the FIFA rankings and featuring several players from the country’s recent World Cup campaign. Ryan Williams put India ahead shortly before half-time, only for Omar Valencia to level with a long-range strike in the second half, leaving Khalid Jamil’s side with an encouraging result against the world No. 44 team.Panama enjoyed more possession during the opening stages, but India stayed compact and looked increasingly dangerous when they broke forward, showing little sign of being overawed by opponents who had competed at the FIFA World Cup only a few months earlier.India created their first clear opening in the eighth minute when Akash Mishra’s cut-back found Williams inside the penalty area, although the forward could not get his shot away. Williams went close again 10 minutes later when he dragged an effort narrowly wide, while Ashique Kuruniyan then found the side-netting as India continued to threaten.The pressure finally produced a breakthrough in the 41st minute. Akash sent a long ball forward, Williams timed his run perfectly to get behind the Panama defence and then kept his composure to beat goalkeeper Marcos Reyes, giving India a 1-0 lead four minutes before the interval.It was a significant moment for a team ranked 138th in the world and playing in Bengaluru for the first time since winning the SAFF Championship at the same stadium in 2023.Panama came out with greater urgency after the restart and quickly began testing the Indian defence. Gurpreet Singh Sandhu was equal to the first major threat, producing a save to deny Giovany Herbert five minutes into the second half.The visitors eventually found their equaliser in the 68th minute, when Valencia struck from outside the box to make it 1-1 and give Panama a platform from which to search for a winner.India still had opportunities to reclaim the lead. Ashique sent a low cross into the box in the 79th minute, but Edmund Lalrindika was unable to make proper contact. Two minutes later, Edmund worked his way in from the right and set up Manvir Singh, who attempted to finish with a backheel rather than taking the simpler option and missed the chance.Panama then pushed forward in search of a decisive goal, striking the woodwork and forcing Gurpreet into another important save. Carlos Harvey, one of the visitors’ World Cup players, also tested the Indian goalkeeper, but India managed to survive the late pressure.Manvir came close again late in the match after being played in by substitute Edmund, while Abhishek Singh Tekcham fired off target following a corner as India continued to carry a threat of their own.The 1-1 draw gives Jamil’s team an important result before a far more demanding sequence of friendlies. India will face five-time world champions Brazil in Kolkata on October 3 before meeting two-time world champions Uruguay at the same venue three days later.For India, the significance of Friday’s result lies not simply in avoiding defeat against Panama, but in the way the Blue Tigers competed against a side ranked 44th in the world. Williams’ first-half finish gave them a lead to protect, Panama eventually found a way through, and India still created enough opportunities afterwards to believe they could have taken all three points.The next two fixtures will provide a considerably tougher test, but the performance in Bengaluru has given Jamil’s side something substantial to carry into them.
Article Summary: India held to 1-1 draw by World Cup-bound Panama. Ryan Williams put India ahead before Omar Valencia equalised. India now turn to Brazil and Uruguay in friendlies. India will face five-time world champions Brazil in Kolkata on October 3.
